Piecewise-linear pulse source. A positive period repeats the pulse; period=0 is a one-shot that returns to v1 after its fall time.

V(t) = offset + amplitude x unit(t). For noise, unit(t) is deterministic zero-mean Gaussian noise updated at 10 kSa/s and held between updates; amplitude is its 1-sigma RMS voltage and the zero-order hold has 5 kHz one-sided equivalent noise bandwidth. rSource is the series output resistance (50 Ω bench default). PWL points are specified as absolute volts using t:v,t:v pairs.

Breakdown voltage set by `vbr` param (default 6.8 V). bidirectional=0 (default) for unidirectional, 1 for symmetric bidirectional clamping. For reverse-overvoltage, the vr_max check is suppressed below vbr — normal operation.

The transient model is ideal inductance in series with winding `dcr`, plus terminal-parallel `coreLossResistance`. Defaults represent a generic 1 mH axial part; use its datasheet values when known. Generic small-signal NPN (2N2222-class). The 75 V Early voltage is a representative fixed forward-active value, not a guaranteed fit for every 2N2222. High-injection beta roll-off, breakdown, junction capacitance, noise and self-heating are not modelled.

Open-collector outputs sink up to 24 mA per segment (datasheet guaranteed; absolute max 40 mA). Use external series resistors (typically 150-470 ohm at 5 V) to limit LED current. Maximum sink voltage 15 V.
Both /PRE and /CLR LOW simultaneously is an undefined state per the TI SN74HC74 datasheet (SCLS108) — Q and /Q both go HIGH while asserted, which is logically inconsistent. Do not rely on this state.
CMOS-4000 logic thresholds are approximately 0.3x and 0.7x Vcc. At 5V: VIL<1.5V, VIH>3.5V. At 10V: VIL<3V, VIH>7V. Source: TI CD4017B datasheet, SCHS027.

CRITICAL DIFFERENCE from 74LS47: outputs are active-HIGH push-pull (not open-collector). Use with common-CATHODE displays. BCD inputs 10-15 produce ALL SEGMENTS BLANK (not partial glyphs like 74LS47). Digit 6: no top bar (a off), no segment b. Digit 9: no bottom bar (d off). Source: TI CD4511B datasheet, SCHS021.

Available outputs with external pins: Q4-Q10, Q12-Q14. Internal stages with NO pins: Q1-Q3, Q11. Oscillator: Rt from RTC (pin 10) to CLK/RS (pin 11), Ct from CTC (pin 9) to CLK/RS (pin 11); f = 1/(2.3 * Rt * Ct); recommend Rt >= 10 kOhm, Ct >= 100 pF. Counter advances on falling edge of CLK/RS (pin 11). CTC (pin 9) = NOT(CLK/RS); RTC (pin 10) = NOT(CTC) = in-phase with CLK/RS. Oscillation emerges from the adaptive transient solve; there is no fixed 50 us engine clock. Solver health and scope effective-rate provenance disclose whether a fast setup is adequately resolved. Source: TI CD4060B datasheet, SCHS007; pin map cross-referenced to Nexperia HEF4060B Rev. 11, Table 2.

4 isolated resistors, each rated 125 mW (0.5 W total package). Tolerance ±5% (same as individual resistors). All four share the single `resistance` param.

Non-polarised; either terminal can connect to the higher-voltage node. The ESR and leakage defaults are representative. Tolerance is typically ±10% for X7R/Y5V dielectrics, better for C0G/NP0. ESR frequency dependence, dielectric absorption, voltage coefficient, and breakdown are not modelled.

Polarised: pin a is positive (+), pin b is negative (−). The ESR and leakage defaults are representative. Tolerance is typically −20%/+80%. Reverse polarity can damage a real part, but polarity damage, ESR frequency/temperature dependence, dielectric absorption, and breakdown are not modelled.

Non-polarised; either terminal can connect to the higher-voltage node. The ESR and leakage defaults are representative. Tolerance is typically ±5–10% for polyester (PET), ±1–2% for polypropylene (PP). ESR frequency dependence, dielectric absorption, and breakdown are not modelled.
Typical contact rating 100 mA at 50 V DC (low-level signal switching only). Contact resistance ≤ 100 mΩ. Insulation resistance ≥ 100 MΩ. Operating life 1 000–10 000 cycles per position.

For an identified PDIP-8 device, solved package power drives a persistent one-pole junction temperature using 80.9 °C/W and an assumed 12 s time constant; the ambient-adjusted power allowance is reported. Temperature does not alter the electrical macro-model, and no reversible thermal shutdown is claimed.

Internal reference voltage Vref=2.495 V (+/-0.5%). Minimum cathode voltage ~2 V (must stay above Vref). Cathode current range 1 mA to 100 mA. REF input draws ~2 µA bias current. Anode = GND-side terminal.

PP3 / 6LR61 alkaline. Runtime charge is coulomb-counted from a 0.55 Ah low-drain reference. Chemistry OCV and internal resistance change with charge; resistance also rises in cold ambient conditions. High-current rate-capacity loss, recovery, self-discharge, aging and self-heating are not modelled.

CR2032 lithium coin cell. Runtime charge is coulomb-counted from a 235 mAh, 15 kΩ / 21 °C reference. Chemistry OCV and internal resistance change with charge; resistance rises strongly in cold ambient conditions. Pulse-load capacity loss, recovery, self-discharge, aging and self-heating are not modelled.

Behavioural non-isolated buck model: IN− and OUT− are one internal return. Within the declared 7–35 V input range, the output regulates at vout (CV), current-limits at iLimit (CC), or follows the averaged maximum-duty ceiling Vout=Vin−vdropout (default 1.5 V). It cannot boost. Present-solve input draw satisfies Iin=Pout/(eta×Vin), including load and regime changes. Below UVLO, above maximum input, or with reversed polarity, it is OFF. Switching ripple and control-loop transients are omitted.

Coil modelled as series R+L (backward-Euler Norton companion). Contact switching uses hysteresis on coil voltage: pull-in when |V_coil| >= vPull, drop-out when |V_coil| < vDrop. Always add a flyback diode across the coil; see the missing-flyback diagnostic.

No VCC pin. Inputs referenced to GND. Output is open-collector sink only; external pull-up or load required for high state. Internal catch diodes from each OUT to COM are electrically modelled and clamp inductive spikes when COM is tied to the load supply rail. Vce_sat is simplified as R_on=5 ohm (approximately 1 V at 200 mA).

8-channel variant of ULN2003A. DIP-18. All electrical characteristics are identical to ULN2003A per channel, including electrically modelled OUT-to-COM catch diodes. Inputs are CMOS/TTL compatible (Vih min 2.5 V, Vil max 1.5 V per ULN2803A datasheet Table 1).

Active buzzer: DC threshold 1.5 V for internal oscillator to run. Passive buzzer: must be driven with an AC/PWM signal; frequency reported from zero-crossing detection. Both types modelled as a fixed resistor (resistance param, default 32 Ω). No audio synthesis — sounding state and detected frequency only.

Passive buzzer: requires AC/PWM drive signal. Frequency detected via zero-crossing counting. Sounding when detected frequency > 0 Hz. Same resistor model as active buzzer (resistance param). No audio synthesis.

Voice coil modelled as pure resistance (8 Ω default). AC reactance of the coil inductance is ignored at audio frequencies for this simplified model. Signal-present detection uses a 5 ms sliding window; peak-to-peak amplitude ≥ 50 mV registers as sounding.

VCC1 (logic, 4.5–7 V) and VCC2/VM (motor rail, 4.5–36 V) are separate supplies. Output stage R_on = 2 Ω per side (1.4 V total drop at 1 A across both output transistors). Internal clamp diodes on each output pin recirculate inductive kickback to VM — suppress missing-flyback when VM is wired. io_max 0.6 A continuous per channel (1.2 A peak).

VCC (logic, 2.7–5.5 V) and VM (motor rail, 2.5–13.5 V) are separate supplies. R_on = 2 Ω per output side (simplified; real device specifies on-resistance as Vce_sat ~0.5 V at 1 A). PWM duty-cycle averaging for speed control is a Wave 7 motor-dynamics feature — in this model PWM is treated as a binary enable: HIGH=active, LOW=coast. Internal freewheeling diodes suppress inductive kickback when VM is wired. io_max 1.2 A continuous per channel.

Winding modelled as series R+L with backward-Euler Norton companion. Back-EMF = Ke × omega opposes applied voltage (motor convention), causing current to decrease as speed rises. Stall current = V / windingR (omega=0). No-load steady-state: omega = (V − R × i_ss) / Ke, i_ss = b × omega_ss / Kt. Rotor dynamics use forward-Euler (stable when h << J/b). omega is a simulator readout and back-EMF driver only — no mechanical coupling to external loads. windingR and windingL must be > 0; inertia must be > 0.

Signal is a truly high-impedance physical input; no 1 MΩ pull-down is present. Solver regularisation of a floating net is numerical only and does not represent a physical load. A falling PWM edge decodes targetAngle from the 1–2 ms pulse, while angle reports the actual shaft position. Actual angle travels without overshoot at 600°/s at 4.8 V and scales linearly with solved supply, giving 625°/s at 5 V. Below the 4.5 V model brownout threshold, velocity becomes zero while targetAngle is retained. At rest, V+ to GND uses idleR=330 Ω. While moving, the 150 mA at 4.8 V teaching assumption becomes a 32 Ω equivalent load. Torque, stall mechanics/current limiting, acceleration, backlash, control hunting, gearbox compliance and heating are not modelled.

Each coil is a series R+L Norton companion (backward-Euler, same as relay coil). No back-EMF in v1. Step detection uses committed current sign post-solve: signA = sign(iA), signB = sign(iB), deadband ±1 mA. Phase sequence: (A+,B+)=0, (A-,B+)=1, (A-,B-)=2, (A+,B-)=3. Sequential phase advance +1 (mod 4) increments position; −1 (mod 4) decrements. Non-sequential jump holds. Stepper coils are inductive — flyback diagnostic fires for bare-transistor drive; suppressed by L293D/TB6612 with VM powered. Unipolar/ULN2003 variant deferred.

Supply modelled as a 150-ohm behavioural load (~33 mA at 5 V) representing a representative lit-matrix draw. Per-LED current accuracy is out of scope for v1; the teaching focus is the decoded pixel pattern. DIN, CLK and CS are high-impedance logic inputs with no invented physical pull-down; an undriven input follows the simulator's disclosed floating-input decision model. Single-device only: DOUT daisy-chain is not modelled. Decode mode must be 0x00 (raw segment bits); BCD mode (0x09) is stored but not rendered.

Supply modelled as a 200-ohm behavioural load (~25 mA at 5 V) representing logic + backlight draw. RS/RW/E/D0-D7 are high-impedance logic inputs with no invented physical pull-down; an undriven input follows the simulator's disclosed floating-input decision model. RW read-back is not supported in v1; tie RW to GND. Custom CGRAM glyphs (codes 0x00-0x07) display as space. Katakana ROM region (0xA0-0xFF) not simulated. HD44780 ROM quirks (0x5C=yen, 0x7E/0x7F=arrows) treated as ASCII. 4-bit and 8-bit modes both supported via function-set DL bit.

Wide-supply model: functional 3.0-5.5 V, matching HC-SR04P and common 3.3 V-tolerant clones. A classic HC-SR04 module is commonly specified 5 V-only, so treat direct 3.3 V operation as clone-dependent on real hardware. Below 3.0 V (VCC-GND) the sensor is inert: ECHO is forced low/hi-Z and TRIG pulses are ignored. TRIG is a 1 MOhm pulldown input, armed by a rising edge; the sensor schedules an echo on the following falling edge (re-triggering while an echo is pending/active is ignored, matching real module behaviour). ECHO timing: rises at trigFall + 250 microseconds, then falls 58.0 microseconds/cm x distanceCm later, or after a 38 millisecond timeout when noEcho (out-of-range) is set. ECHO drives push-pull to the sensor's own committed VCC through the house 50 ohm gate output resistance.
